segmentation.text: No motorcycle or motor scooter
shall be ridden upon any sidewalk
of the City

elements.justification: 'motorcycle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-135::motorcycle ('every motor vehicle equipped with a seat or saddle for the use of the driver and designed to travel on not more than three wheels in contact with the ground, excluding an electric bicycle, a tractor or a moped'), claimed as one atom and never expanded. 'motor scooter' has no applicable definition and the table admits no aggregate for it, so its ordinary words, a scooter propelled by a motor, are carried by the class atoms whose contracts denote such machines: ru.moped ('a low-power two- or three-wheeler with a small engine or motor', the class whose corpus definition names a 'motor-driven scooter') and ru.electric_scooter ('a standing or seated electric scooter with handlebars'); a motor scooter above the moped class is a motor vehicle on not more than three wheels with a seat, so already a member of the motorcycle aggregate. ru.pedestrian is not read: its contract is 'Not a stand-in for: a person on a bicycle or scooter'. 'No' states the prohibition the obligation span carries.

st.sidewalk is the 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line', the extent of DEF-NRS-484A-240 ('that portion of a highway between the curb lines or the lateral lines of a highway and the adjacent property lines intended for the use of pedestrians'); its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: a crosswalk' is kept: a crosswalk is not read as a sidewalk. rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') anchors 'upon' to the subject's own sidewalk, and 'any' makes every sidewalk region count. 'be ridden' is the machine's controlled motion, drv.motion.moving (speed above the source's resolution), under the agency reading disclosed below.

assumptions.meaning: The place of the observation lies inside the territorial limits of an incorporated city, as declared for the map or the trace.

applicability: x is a motorcycle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-135::motorcycle), a moped (ru.moped) or an electric scooter (ru.electric_scooter), and asm.within_city_limits holds at the observation.
obligation: At the observation, x is not both moving (drv.motion.moving(x) with speed_floor p.speed_resolution) and occupying (rel.occupies) any st.sidewalk region.

narrowings.why: 'be ridden' is read through the machine's controlled motion: a motorcycle or scooter moving above the speed resolution while its footprint overlaps a sidewalk is taken to be ridden there, one standing still is not; who or what is at the controls is not observed.

segmentation.text: The following regulations pertain to the operation of
vehicles
within a roundabout
All vehicular travel shall be in a counterclockwise direction

elements.justification: 'vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', with its exceptions), claimed as one atom.

st.roundabout is 'a rotary intersection: its central island, its circulatory roadway and its entry and exit approaches', which denotes DEF-LVMC-11-02-130 ('an intersection characterized by a circulatory roadway, channelized approaches and yield control of entering traffic', encompassing 'the area bounded by the outermost curb line' and including 'the crosswalks on any entering or exiting roadway': the entry and exit approaches the contract names). rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') anchors 'within' to the roundabout the vehicle is in.

'vehicular travel' is the motion of the vehicle the subject span binds (the same aggregate). 'in a counterclockwise direction' is the sense of that motion about the roundabout: drv.motion.clockwise_about_region reads the vector from the region's reference point (st.region_geometry, 'the reference point and the boundary polygon of a structure region in the world frame') to the vehicle's position (kin.position) against its velocity (kin.velocity, 'velocity vector', world frame) and speed (kin.speed); its own exclusion makes it no stand-in for travel against a lane direction, so no lane marking or st.lane_direction is read. The duty is violated by clockwise motion; motion toward or away from the centre (entering, leaving) and standstill are neither sense and do not violate it.

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and occupies (rel.occupies) some st.roundabout region at the observation.
obligation: For every st.roundabout region r that x occupies at the observation, x is not moving clockwise about r: not drv.motion.clockwise_about_region(x, r) with speed_floor p.speed_resolution and sine_tolerance p.circulation_sine_tolerance.

narrowings.why: 'counterclockwise' is read as the sense of the vehicle's motion about the roundabout region's reference point (st.region_geometry), taken as the centre its circulatory roadway runs around, viewed from above; the duty is judged by the absence of the opposite (clockwise) sense, so a vehicle at rest or moving radially within the tolerance (entering or leaving) complies.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
about to enter or exit a controlled-access highway
shall yield the right-of-way
to all vehicles approaching on the highway
whose proximity constitutes an immediate hazard
and shall continue to yield the right-of-way
to that traffic
until the driver may proceed with reasonable safety.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'the driver' is read through its controlled motion.

'a controlled-access highway' is st.controlled_access 'a highway with access only at designated points' (DEF-NRS-484A-060 'no legal right of access except at such points only'). 'about to enter or exit' is read by the movement it leads to: the footprint beginning to overlap the region (drv.motion.entering_region) or ceasing to (drv.motion.leaving_region), through rel.occupies.
'shall yield the right-of-way' (DEF-NRS-484A-210 'to proceed ... in preference'): x does not make the entry or the exit while a vehicle owed precedence is a hazard.

'all vehicles' are the admitted aggregate; 'approaching on the highway': y occupies the controlled-access region (rel.occupies) and is moving (drv.motion.moving over kin.speed); its approach toward x is read by the standard's closest approach.

operationalizations.standard: proximity that constitutes an immediate hazard
operationalizations.convention: Surrogate safety conflict (FHWA SSAM; critical gap as the horizon): y's centre is predicted, under constant velocities, to come within p.conflict_clearance of x's within p.immediate_hazard_gap. The primitives alone are not a stand-in for contact or the danger of a crash; the bound is the standard's.

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and at this observation enters (drv.motion.entering_region x a) or leaves (drv.motion.leaving_region x a) a region a of kind st.controlled_access.
obligation: At this entry or exit no vehicle y other than x (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) occupies a (rel.occupies y a), is moving (drv.motion.moving y with p.speed_resolution) and is in predicted conflict with x: prim.closest_approach_within x y with horizon p.immediate_hazard_gap and prim.closest_approach_distance x y with the same horizon below p.conflict_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
'about to enter or exit' is an imminent movement, read by the entry into or the exit from the controlled-access region it leads to.
The yield is judged at the entry or exit observation: making it while a hazard exists is the failure to yield.

segmentation.text: Every vehicle driven
upon a divided highway
must be driven only upon the right-hand roadway
and
must not be driven over, across or within any dividing space, barrier or section or make any left turn, semicircular turn or U-turn
except through an opening in the barrier or dividing section or space
or at a crossover or intersection
established by a public authority

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom; 'driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading below).

A divided highway is 'a highway divided into two or more roadways by means of a physical barrier or dividing section' (DEF-NRS-484A-070): an st.highway ('the entire public way between its boundary lines') on which (st.on_way) an st.median_or_divider lies ('physical barrier or dividing section between roadways'), its parts being st.roadway regions ('separate roadways of a divided highway are separate'). 'upon' is x's footprint overlapping (rel.occupies) a roadway or dividing section lying on that highway; st.highway's exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: the roadway' is respected: the roadway is read as the part of the way it is.

The roadways of a divided highway each carry one direction; st.lane_direction is the 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in — ... a roadway, one-way roadway'. The right-hand roadway, under right-hand traffic, is the one whose designated direction is the vehicle's direction of travel, so being driven upon another roadway of the highway is moving against the designated direction of the roadway x occupies: drv.motion.against_carrier_direction(x, r), from kin.velocity and kin.speed. The concept is 'Not a stand-in for' the heading opposing the carrier, so a vehicle crossing a roadway at a wide angle is not driven upon it against its direction.

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and occupies (rel.occupies) an st.roadway or st.median_or_divider region lying on (st.on_way) an st.highway region h on which some st.median_or_divider region lies.
obligation: Re-binding h with the same selection: for every st.roadway region r lying on h that x occupies at the observation, x does not move against r's designated direction: not drv.motion.against_carrier_direction(x, r) with speed_floor p.speed_resolution and opposed_cosine p.opposed_direction_cosine.

narrowings.why: 'driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle moving on the highway is taken to be driven, whoever or whatever controls it.

'the right-hand roadway' is read as the roadway whose designated direction (st.lane_direction) is the vehicle's direction of travel, as right-hand traffic makes it; 'only upon' is read as the choice between the highway's roadways, so this node judges travel against a roadway's direction; driving over or within the dividing section is the second obligation of the line, and crossing a roadway at a wider angle than the tolerance is not driving upon it.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
shall not overtake and pass another vehicle upon the right
when such movement requires driving off the paved portion of the highway

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom. 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080, 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle') is a relational role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading below).

'another vehicle' is a road user of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle other than the subject, quantified because it is present only sometimes. 'overtake and pass ... upon the right' is drv.interaction.passing_on_right(x, y): headings aligned (rel.same_direction), bodies side by side along x's heading (rel.longitudinal_overlap, 'the bodies overlap along the subject's heading (side by side)'), y on x's left (rel.bearing, 'for "on the right of"'), x faster than y (kin.speed). rel.longitudinal_overlap is 'neither a contact nor a distance between the bodies' and is read only as side-by-side.

The paved portion of the highway (DEF-NRS-484A-095, 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way') is told from the unpaved by the paved attributes the ontology carries: st.shoulder 'the part of the highway beside the roadway not intended for vehicular traffic; paved attribute' and st.road_edge 'curb or edge of the roadway; paved attribute for the surface beyond it'. 'driving off the paved portion' is x's footprint overlapping (rel.occupies) a shoulder whose paved attribute is false, or a road edge whose surface beyond is unpaved. 'such movement requires' is read by the movement as made: the pass that is made with the vehicle off the pavement at the same observation is the one the words name.

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and, at the observation, x is off the paved portion of the highway: it occupies (rel.occupies) a st.shoulder region whose paved attribute is false, or a st.road_edge whose paved attribute (the surface beyond it) is false.
obligation: At the observation there is no road user y other than x that is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and that x is passing on y's right: not drv.interaction.passing_on_right(x, y) with aligned_cosine p.same_direction_cosine and speed_margin p.overtaking_speed_margin.

narrowings.why: 'The driver of a vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, and the duty binds that vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.

'overtake and pass' is judged at the side-by-side phase of the movement (drv.interaction.passing_on_right): an approach from behind on the unpaved surface that never comes alongside, and the return ahead of the other vehicle after the bodies no longer overlap, are not judged by this node.
'driving' off the pavement is read through the vehicle's controlled motion over the unpaved surface, whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: branch_1

segmentation.text: Every vehicle driven
upon a divided highway
must be driven only upon the right-hand roadway
and
must not be driven over, across or within any dividing space, barrier or section or make any left turn, semicircular turn or U-turn
except through an opening in the barrier or dividing section or space
or at a crossover or intersection
established by a public authority

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom; 'driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading below).

A divided highway is 'a highway divided into two or more roadways by means of a physical barrier or dividing section' (DEF-NRS-484A-070): an st.highway ('the entire public way between its boundary lines') on which (st.on_way) an st.median_or_divider lies ('physical barrier or dividing section between roadways'), its parts being st.roadway regions ('separate roadways of a divided highway are separate'). 'upon' is x's footprint overlapping (rel.occupies) a roadway or dividing section lying on that highway; st.highway's exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: the roadway' is respected: the roadway is read as the part of the way it is.

'any dividing space, barrier or section' is the st.median_or_divider, 'physical barrier or dividing section between roadways', lying on the divided highway; 'driven over, across or within' it is x's footprint overlapping it (rel.occupies) at any observation: on it, crossing it or standing within it. On a divided highway a left, semicircular or U-turn made off an opening, crossover or intersection shows in its outcome: a left turn from a roadway crosses the dividing section on its left (st.median_or_divider, rel.occupies), and a semicircular or U-turn, 'the turning of a vehicle upon a highway so as to proceed in the opposite direction' (DEF-NRS-484B-077), either crosses it or leaves the vehicle proceeding against the designated direction (st.lane_direction) of the roadway it occupies: drv.motion.against_carrier_direction(x, r), from kin.velocity and kin.speed. The concept is 'Not a stand-in for' the heading opposing the carrier, so a vehicle backing is read by its motion.

st.median_or_divider carries an 'opening attribute where a crossover exists': 'an opening in the barrier or dividing section or space' is the dividing-section region carrying that attribute, and 'through' it is x's footprint overlapping (rel.occupies) such a region.

'a crossover' is the same opening of the dividing section (st.median_or_divider, 'opening attribute where a crossover exists'); 'intersection' is st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet', which with DEF-NRS-484A-105 (2) makes 'every crossing of each roadway of such divided highway by an intersecting highway ... a separate intersection'. 'at' is x's footprint overlapping (rel.occupies) such an opening or intersection.

'established by a public authority' (DEF-NRS-484A-195, 'the Department of Transportation or the local authority having jurisdiction') is the legal status of the opening, crossover or intersection; its presence on the road (an st.median_or_divider region with the opening attribute, an st.intersection) is the evidence of that status (status reading below).

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and occupies (rel.occupies) an st.roadway or st.median_or_divider region lying on (st.on_way) an st.highway region h on which some st.median_or_divider region lies.
obligation: Re-binding h with the same selection: at the observation, unless x occupies an st.median_or_divider region lying on h that carries the opening attribute, or occupies an st.intersection region lying on h, neither (a) x occupies an st.median_or_divider region lying on h, nor (b) x occupies an st.roadway region r lying on h and moves against its designated direction: drv.motion.against_carrier_direction(x, r) with speed_floor p.speed_resolution and opposed_cosine p.opposed_direction_cosine.

narrowings.why: 'driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle moving on the highway is taken to be driven, whoever or whatever controls it.

The left, semicircular and U-turns are read through their outcome on the divided highway, not as manoeuvres recognized from the heading: crossing the dividing section, or proceeding against the designated direction of the roadway occupied ('so as to proceed in the opposite direction'); a left turn that leaves the roadway on its left without touching the dividing section is not read, and a vehicle travelling against a roadway's direction without having turned is judged here too.
'established by a public authority' is read through the presence of the opening, crossover or intersection on the road: the feature's presence is the evidence of its establishment.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
Shall not back into an intersection, on or over a crosswalk, or around a
street
corner

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom. 'driver' is no aggregate: DEF-NRS-484A-080 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle' names a relational role, read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading below), so the duty binds the vehicle's conduct.

Three alternatives of one prohibition. (1) 'back into an intersection': st.intersection is 'the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges; a junction where an alley meets another way ... is no intersection', which denotes DEF-NRS-484A-105 (1) 'the area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines' and (3) 'The junction of an alley with a street, road or highway shall not constitute an intersection'; its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: a crosswalk or a stop line' is kept: entry into the intersection region itself is read. 'back' is drv.motion.reversing (velocity along heading below minus the resolution, never kin.gear, which is 'Not a stand-in for: the direction of motion'). 'into' is the observation at which x's footprint begins to overlap the intersection (rel.occupies rising) while reversing. (2) 'on or over a crosswalk': st.crosswalk is the 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection', which denotes both limbs of DEF-NRS-484A-065 ('That part of a highway at an intersection included within the connections of the lateral lines of the sidewalks' and 'Any portion of a highway at an intersection or elsewhere distinctly indicated for pedestrian crossing'). 'on or over' is x's footprint overlapping the crosswalk (rel.occupies) at an observation at which x is reversing (drv.motion.reversing): on it, or passing over it. (3) 'around a' corner, said of backing, is reversing (drv.motion.reversing, from kin.velocity and kin.heading) while the heading changes (drv.motion.yawing, the absolute kin.yaw_rate above the resolution: 'rate of change of heading'); kin.yaw_rate's exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: road curvature' is respected: the vehicle's own heading change is read, not the road's shape.

A street corner is the corner where ways meet: read as the st.intersection region ('the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges'), whose corners are where the curb lines prolonged by DEF-NRS-484A-105 meet; rel.occupies anchors the backing vehicle to it. The highway part of DEF-NRS-484A-265 ('the entire width between the boundary lines of every highway ... open to the use of the public for purposes of vehicular traffic') is the ways the intersection lies on; its city part is carried by the assumption on 'street'.

assumptions.meaning: The place of the observation lies inside the territorial limits of an incorporated city, as declared for the map or the trace.

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle).
obligation: At the observation none of the following holds: (a) x is reversing (drv.motion.reversing(x), speed_floor p.speed_resolution) and its footprint begins here to overlap (rel.occupies rising) some st.intersection region; (b) x is reversing and occupies (rel.occupies) some st.crosswalk region; (c) asm.within_city_limits holds, x is reversing and yawing (drv.motion.yawing(x), yaw_floor p.yaw_rate_resolution), and x occupies some st.intersection region.

narrowings.why: 'The driver of a vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, and the duty binds that vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.

segmentation.text: A pedestrian
walking or otherwise traveling on a sidewalk
who encounters an obstruction to his or her mobility on the sidewalk,
including, without limitation, a short section of the sidewalk that is missing or impassable,
may proceed
with due care
on the immediately adjacent highway to move around such an obstruction.
Such a pedestrian:
(a) Must walk or otherwise travel as far to the side of the highway near the sidewalk
as possible;
(b) May walk or otherwise travel on the highway in the direction he or she was walking or traveling on the sidewalk, regardless of the direction of traffic;
(c) May walk or otherwise travel in a lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters
if the area between the lane and the sidewalk is impassable;
and
(d) Must return to the sidewalk
as soon as practicable.

elements.justification: 'pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian.
As in NRS_484B_297_6_o1: rel.occupies of a st.sidewalk while moving.
As in NRS_484B_297_6_o1: a st.obstruction within the encounter reach (st.region_geometry) while on the sidewalk.
As in NRS_484B_297_6_o1: nearest atoms with a gap.
'may proceed': on the highway the sidewalk lies on (st.on_way), off every sidewalk (rel.occupies).
As in NRS_484B_297_6_o1.
'Such a pedestrian' refers back to the pedestrian of the admitted aggregate in that situation.
'return to the sidewalk': the pedestrian's footprint overlaps a st.sidewalk again (rel.occupies).

operationalizations.convention: Return time (a few steps at the HCM design walking speed): once no obstruction lies within p.obstruction_encounter_reach of the pedestrian (st.region_geometry distance to every st.obstruction), the return to the sidewalk is made within p.sidewalk_return_time.

residues.why: A permission to travel against the direction of traffic; the duty to return to the sidewalk is the same whichever way the pedestrian walks.

obligation: Within p.sidewalk_return_time ahead (a .time window), x occupies a sidewalk (rel.occupies x w2, w2 of kind st.sidewalk) at some observation.

narrowings.why: 'to move around such an obstruction' is read through leaving the sidewalk where the obstruction was encountered and staying off it since.

'as soon as practicable' is read as one fixed return time counted from the observations at which no obstruction is within reach; whether the sidewalk beside the pedestrian is passable there is not read.

segmentation.text: The operator of a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
shall not: Overtake and pass a motor vehicle
unless the operator can do so safely without endangering himself or herself or the occupants of the motor vehicle.

elements.justification: The three machines are the admitted aggregates of the definitions that apply: DEF-NRS-484A-025 ("a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride"), DEF-NRS-484B-017 ("a device upon which a person may ride, having two or three wheels") and DEF-NRS-484B-018 ("a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor"). ru.aggregate: "membership of a legal aggregate"; each is claimed by its admitted id and never expanded into class atoms. 'The operator of' names who controls the machine, a role and not a membership, read through the machine's controlled motion (observable_reading agency).

Overtaking and passing is the manoeuvre the proposed concept drv.interaction.overtaking_alongside denotes in its side-by-side phase: "Road user x is overtaking road user y alongside at the observation: the side-by-side phase of an overtaking, on either side of y". The words name no side, so the concept counts either side (unlike drv.interaction.passing_on_right). Its atoms rel.same_direction, rel.longitudinal_overlap and kin.speed are claimed as the concept reads them; rel.longitudinal_overlap is 'not a stand-in' for contact or a distance and is used for neither. 'a motor vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ("every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails"; "does not include an electric bicycle or an electric scooter"), which the road user overtaken, quantified in the rule, must carry; it is never replaced by ru.motor_vehicle.

operationalizations.standard: safely without endangering himself or herself or the occupants of the motor vehicle
operationalizations.convention: Passing-clearance convention for cycles passing motor vehicles (the endangerment of the occupants and of the rider by the vehicle passed): the surface gap between the two bodies while side by side is at least the passing clearance, read by its degree. Surrogate-safety closest-approach convention (the endangerment of the rider by other traffic): no other road user is predicted, under constant velocities within the critical gap, to come nearer the rider than the conflict radius.

applicability: x carries ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, and at the observation some road user y other than x that carries ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle is being overtaken alongside by x (drv.interaction.overtaking_alongside(x, y) with p.same_direction_cosine and p.overtaking_speed_margin).
obligation: For every road user y other than x that carries ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle and that x is overtaking alongside at the observation: the surface gap between x and y (rel.surface_gap) is at least p.passing_lateral_clearance; and for every road user z other than x and y it is not the case that x and z approach each other within p.immediate_hazard_gap (prim.closest_approach_within) with a closest-approach centre distance (prim.closest_approach_distance) below p.conflict_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'The operator' is read through the machine's controlled motion: the duty binds the conduct of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter whoever controls it.

'Overtake and pass' is judged in its side-by-side phase, where the clearance to the vehicle passed and the exposure to other traffic arise; the approach from behind and the return ahead are not judged on their own.

'safely without endangering himself or herself or the occupants of the motor vehicle' is read through two contracts only: the surface gap kept to the motor vehicle passed (the exposure of its occupants and of the rider to that vehicle) and the predicted closest approach to every other road user (the rider's exposure to other traffic). The road surface, the sight available and the rider's balance are not read.

param_proposals.convention: Conflict radius: the centre distance at predicted closest approach below which two road users' paths count as in conflict; about the half-length plus half-width of two passenger cars.

param_proposals.source: Highway Capacity Manual critical-gap values

segmentation.text: Upon any highway
outside of a business or residence district
no person shall stop, park or leave standing
any vehicle, whether attended or unattended,
upon the paved or main-traveled part of the highway
when it is practicable to stop, park or so leave such vehicle off such part of the highway,
but in every event
an unobstructed width of the highway
opposite a standing vehicle
shall be left for the free passage of other vehicles
and
a clear view of such stopped vehicles shall be available from a distance of 200 feet in each direction upon such highway.

This section shall not apply to the driver of any vehicle which is disabled while on the paved or main-traveled portion of a highway in such manner and to such extent that it is impossible to avoid stopping and temporarily leaving such disabled vehicle in such position.

elements.justification: st.highway: "the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders"; x is upon it where its footprint overlaps it (rel.occupies).
'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed by id; 'whether attended or unattended' excludes no member.

'such stopped vehicles' are those of the first clause, upon the paved or main-traveled part: the st.roadway ("the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder"), overlapped by x's footprint (rel.occupies).

A stopped vehicle is x halted (drv.motion.halted, kin.speed at or below the resolution); the stop is not a prohibited one here, so the definition of stopping when prohibited adds no exclusion. A clear view of it from a distance along the highway is st.sight_distance at its place: "the distance along the road within which a vehicle at a point and another vehicle on the road could see each other ... both the view of approaching traffic from that point and its being seen by drivers approaching it"; it is at least the law's literal. It is 'not a stand-in' for whether an actual road user saw x (rel.visible), and is not used as one.

A vehicle disabled on the roadway is read through its nearest observables, as in the first obligation of this line: engine or motor not running (kin.engine_running: "so that propulsion is available", false) with hazard lamps flashing (sig.hazard: "both indicators flashing together"), while it occupies the roadway (rel.occupies, st.roadway). kin.engine_running is 'not a stand-in' for motion or a halt; the gap records that the disability itself has no atom.

assumptions.meaning: The place of the observation lies inside a business district or a residence district declared for the map or the trace.

applicability: x carries ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; at the observation x is halted (drv.motion.halted with p.speed_resolution) with its footprint overlapping a st.roadway of a st.highway (rel.occupies); asm.within_business_or_residence_district does not hold; and x is not disabled there: not (kin.engine_running false and sig.hazard on).
obligation: The sight distance at x's place (st.sight_distance) is at least the literal of span g12.

narrowings.why: 'in each direction' is read through the sight distance the source reports for the place, which states both the view from it and its being seen along the road without separating the two directions of the way.
The sight distance at x's place is read off the roadway regions x occupies, and is required at each of them where x straddles several.

outside of a business or residence district
no person shall stop, park or leave standing
any vehicle, whether attended or unattended,

elements.justification: st.highway: "the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders" (DEF-NRS-484A-095, "the entire width between the boundary lines of every way"); x is upon it where its footprint overlaps it (rel.occupies).

'stop', prohibited here, takes DEF-NRS-484A-260 ("any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device"); 'park' (DEF-NRS-484A-155, "the standing of a vehicle") and 'leave standing' (DEF-NRS-484A-250, "the halting of a vehicle") are halts too. The halt is drv.motion.halted ("speed ... at or below speed_floor ... with no minimum duration", kin.speed), which observes any halting, even momentary. The definition's exclusions are carried beside it: a halt behind another road user ahead in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) within the conflict standoff gap (rel.surface_gap) avoids a conflict; a halt while a police officer's stop direction (dev.human_direction, indication stop) or a signal showing a red indication or a stop sign (dev.traffic_signal, dev.stop_sign) governs (dev.governs) the travel region x occupies is in compliance with directions. Purposes of parking and standing (loading, passengers) are not observable and are read through the halt (observable_reading purpose).
'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed by id; 'whether attended or unattended' excludes no member.

The paved or main-traveled part of the highway is the st.roadway ("the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder"; DEF-NRS-484A-220, "that portion of a highway which is improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder"); x halts upon it where its footprint overlaps it (rel.occupies). A paved shoulder is off it: the words set the main-traveled part against the part off it where the vehicle may be left. st.roadway is 'not a stand-in' for the sidewalk.

A vehicle disabled on the roadway so that stopping cannot be avoided is read through its nearest observables, the same as the earlier mapping of 'a disabled vehicle' in this iteration: its engine or motor not running, so that propulsion is unavailable (kin.engine_running: "the vehicle's engine or motor is running, so that propulsion is available", false), with its hazard lamps flashing (sig.hazard: "both indicators flashing together"), while it occupies the roadway (rel.occupies, st.roadway). kin.engine_running is 'not a stand-in' for motion or a halt, and is not used as either; the gap records that the disability itself has no atom.

operationalizations.standard: practicable to stop, park or so leave such vehicle off such part of the highway
operationalizations.convention: Off-road stopping convention: moving off the main-traveled part is practicable where a shoulder lies within the reach of a short lateral move from the halted vehicle's body; the ground distance from the body to the nearest shoulder is the measured magnitude compared with the reach.

assumptions.meaning: The place of the observation lies inside a business district or a residence district declared for the map or the trace.

applicability: x carries ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; at the observation x's footprint overlaps a st.highway (rel.occupies) and asm.within_business_or_residence_district does not hold; and x is not disabled there: not (kin.engine_running false and sig.hazard on while x occupies a st.roadway).
obligation: It is not the case that, at the observation, x is halted (drv.motion.halted with p.speed_resolution) with its footprint overlapping a st.roadway, while some st.shoulder lies within p.offroad_stop_reach of x's body (st.region_geometry distance), unless the halt falls under the exclusions of the defined 'stop': some other road user is ahead of x in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with a surface gap (rel.surface_gap) at most p.stopping_conflict_gap, or a dev.human_direction with indication stop, a dev.traffic_signal displaying circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red, or a dev.stop_sign governs (dev.governs) a travel region x occupies.

narrowings.why: 'stop, park or leave standing' are read through the halt itself; the purposes that set parking and standing apart (loading, receiving passengers) are not observable, and every halt is a stop under the definition that applies, so none is lost.
'practicable' is read through the distance to a shoulder only; the shoulder's width, surface and load-bearing are not read.

segmentation.text: Upon any highway
outside of a business or residence district
no person shall stop, park or leave standing
any vehicle, whether attended or unattended,
upon the paved or main-traveled part of the highway
when it is practicable to stop, park or so leave such vehicle off such part of the highway,
but in every event
an unobstructed width of the highway
opposite a standing vehicle
shall be left for the free passage of other vehicles
and
a clear view of such stopped vehicles shall be available from a distance of 200 feet in each direction upon such highway.

This section shall not apply to the driver of any vehicle which is disabled while on the paved or main-traveled portion of a highway in such manner and to such extent that it is impossible to avoid stopping and temporarily leaving such disabled vehicle in such position.

elements.justification: st.highway: "the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders"; x is upon it where its footprint overlaps it (rel.occupies).
'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed by id; 'whether attended or unattended' excludes no member.

The standing vehicles 'in every event' are those of the first clause, upon the paved or main-traveled part: the st.roadway ("the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder"), overlapped by x's footprint (rel.occupies).

A width of the highway opposite the vehicle is a lane beside it: a st.lane ("a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles") on the same highway (st.on_way, st.highway) whose ground distance from x's body (st.region_geometry) is at most the beside reach, so that a lane segment far along the way is not read, and that x's footprint does not overlap (rel.occupies). Unobstructed: no other halted road user beside x occupies it.

'a standing vehicle' (DEF-NRS-484A-250, "the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not") is x halted (drv.motion.halted, kin.speed at or below the resolution); its purpose is not observable (observable_reading purpose). Opposite it is the stretch alongside its body: another halted road user is opposite where their footprints overlap along x's heading (rel.longitudinal_overlap positive), a projection, 'not' a contact or a distance.

A vehicle disabled on the roadway is read through its nearest observables, as in the first obligation of this line: engine or motor not running (kin.engine_running: "so that propulsion is available", false) with hazard lamps flashing (sig.hazard: "both indicators flashing together"), while it occupies the roadway (rel.occupies, st.roadway). kin.engine_running is 'not a stand-in' for motion or a halt; the gap records that the disability itself has no atom.

operationalizations.standard: an unobstructed width left for the free passage of other vehicles
operationalizations.convention: Free-passage convention: the width left for passage is a lane beside the standing vehicle, not overlapped by it and not taken by another halted road user alongside it, whose measured width (st.lane_width) is at least a design passenger-car width plus lateral clearance.

assumptions.meaning: The place of the observation lies inside a business district or a residence district declared for the map or the trace.

applicability: x carries ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; at the observation x is halted (drv.motion.halted with p.speed_resolution) with its footprint overlapping a st.roadway of a st.highway h (rel.occupies, st.on_way); asm.within_business_or_residence_district does not hold; and x is not disabled there: not (kin.engine_running false and sig.hazard on).
obligation: Some st.lane L on h (st.on_way(L, h)) that x's footprint does not overlap, within p.opposite_lane_reach of x's body (st.region_geometry distance), has st.lane_width at least p.free_passage_width, and no road user other than x that is halted (drv.motion.halted with p.speed_resolution) and overlaps x along x's heading (rel.longitudinal_overlap positive) occupies L.

narrowings.why: 'an unobstructed width of the highway' is read as a whole lane beside the vehicle, free of halted road users alongside it; a part-lane, a shoulder, or an obstruction that is not a road user (st.obstruction) is not counted.

segmentation.text: If a highway has been designed to provide
a single right lane to be used only for turning
a vehicle must
While being driven in the right turn lane
not travel through an intersection

elements.justification: st.highway is 'the entire public way between its boundary lines', denoting DEF-NRS-484A-095 ('the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority ...'); st.on_way ('the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on — a lane, roadway, ...') ties the turn lane to that highway. 'has been designed to provide' is the lane's presence on the map (status reading below).

st.turn_lane is 'a lane designated only for turning; side ∈ {left, right}', with side right: 'a ... right lane to be used only for turning'. 'single' is read as no neighbouring lane being a right turn lane too: st.lane_adjacency gives the 'left / right neighbouring lane of the same direction' (its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: the marking between two lanes' is respected: lanes, not markings, are compared), so a pair of adjacent right turn lanes is not a single one.
'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom; 'must' introduces the duty the obligation span states.

'the right turn lane' is the lane L the condition singles out (st.turn_lane, side right); 'being driven in' it is x's footprint overlapping it (rel.occupies), read at the observation at which x's footprint begins to overlap the intersection: the moment the travel through begins.

'an intersection' is the st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges', DEF-NRS-484A-105) the turn lane runs into (st.lane_enters, 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'); a turn lane reaches no other. 'travel through' it is entering it from the lane and leaving it (rel.occupies rising, then falling) without the heading change of a right turn: drv.motion.heading_change_since_entry (from kin.yaw_rate, left positive; 'Not a stand-in for: road curvature' is respected, the vehicle's own heading change over the passage is read) not reaching minus the turn recognition angle by the exit.

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and x occupies (rel.occupies) at the observation, or occupied at an earlier observation, a single right turn lane L: an st.turn_lane region of side right lying on (st.on_way) an st.highway region, with no lane adjacent to it (st.lane_adjacency) that is also an st.turn_lane of side right.
obligation: Re-binding L with the same selection and I as the st.intersection region L enters (st.lane_enters): at the observation it is not the case that x stops here occupying I (rel.occupies of x and I false here and true at the previous observation), having begun to overlap I at an observation at which it occupied L, with its heading change since that entry (drv.motion.heading_change_since_entry(x, I), step p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph) greater than minus p.turn_recognition_angle.

narrowings.why: 'has been designed to provide' is read through the lane's presence as mapped: a right turn lane on the highway evidences the design.
'being driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion in the lane, whoever or whatever controls it.

'travel through an intersection' is read as entering the intersection from the turn lane and leaving it without turning right: a straight passage and a left turn alike; a passage still under way when the recording ends is not decided.

param_proposals.convention: Turn recognition: the heading change through an intersection beyond which a passage counts as a turn rather than a straight crossing; half the right angle of a turn at a right-angled junction, leaving room for skewed junctions and lane offsets.

segmentation.text: A signal of intention to turn right or left, or otherwise turn a vehicle from a direct course, shall be given continuously during not less than the last 100 feet traveled
in a business or residential district
and not less than the last 300 feet traveled
in any other area
prior to changing the course
of a vehicle.
This rule shall be observed, regardless of the weather.

elements.justification: A signal of intention to turn is the signal itself, not a declared intention (the ontology: "a signal 'of intention' is the signal"): sig.turn_indicator ("the turn indicator state ∈ {off, left, right}") or sig.hand_signal ("a driver's or rider's arm signal; meaning ∈ {no_signal, left, right, stop_or_slow, re_enter}") showing the side of the change of course; sig.turn_indicator is 'not a stand-in' for the turn itself, which is read separately. A direct course is travel along the designated direction of the carrier x occupies (rel.occupies a st.travel_region carrying st.lane_direction); turning right or left or otherwise from it is x's velocity departing to one side of that direction, the proposed concepts drv.motion.veering_left and drv.motion.veering_right ("it moves forward along the carrier while its velocity points to the left [right] of the carrier's direction by more than a tolerance", from kin.velocity and kin.speed); following a bend of the carrier is not a departure, since the designated direction bends with it. 'given continuously during not less than the last 100 feet traveled' is a window measured in distance travelled (a .path window, which reads kin.path_length: "distance travelled along the body's path since the start of the trace, monotone") at every observation of which the signal of the departure's side is shown; the figure is the law's literal.
The same .path window (kin.path_length) with the law's other literal, the bound selected where the place is not in a business or residence district (span f7).

Changing the course is the observation at which a departure to one side begins: drv.motion.veering_left or drv.motion.veering_right holds for a carrier x occupies (rel.occupies) and held for none at the observation before. The signal window ends there.

'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway"), claimed by id: the subject x whose course changes.

assumptions.meaning: The place of the observation lies inside a business district or a residence district declared for the map or the trace.
The place of the observation lies inside a business district or a residence district declared for the map or the trace.

residues.why: The duty is the same in every weather: the words exclude no weather and add no condition, so no environment atom is read.

applicability: x carries ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle and at the observation begins a change of course: for some travel region c that x occupies (rel.occupies), drv.motion.veering_left(x, c) or drv.motion.veering_right(x, c) (with p.speed_resolution and p.course_departure_sine) holds there, and at the observation before neither held for any region x occupied.
obligation: For a departure to the left, x showed a left signal (sig.turn_indicator left, or sig.hand_signal left) at every observation of the window behind the observation measured in x's distance travelled (.path, kin.path_length), whose length is the literal of span f1 where asm.within_business_or_residence_district holds at the observation and the literal of span f6 where it does not (a bound selected by the condition); for a departure to the right, the right signal likewise. A departure to both sides at once owes the signal of either.

narrowings.why: 'otherwise turn a vehicle from a direct course' is read as the velocity departing to one side of the designated direction of the carrier the vehicle occupies, on lanes, roadways and other carriers that carry a direction; a turn begun where the vehicle occupies only an intersection, which carries no direction, is not recognized.

segmentation.text: It is unlawful for the driver of any vehicle:
When crossing at grade any track or tracks of a railroad,

to fail to completely cross the track or tracks without stopping due to insufficient: (1) Space for the vehicle on the opposite side of the railroad crossing; or (2) Undercarriage clearance of the vehicle.

As used in this section, “completely cross” means to travel across a railroad track or tracks in such a manner that the trailing end of the vehicle is 15 feet or more past the nearest rail of the railroad track or tracks.

elements.justification: “vehicle” is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines, admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, so it is claimed as one atom, ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle: “membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id”; the reading classifies the classes under it by the definition's words “every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway, except: (1) Devices moved by human power or used exclusively upon stationary rails; (2) Electric bicycles; ... (4) An electric scooter”, so its exclusions are the reading's and are not expanded here. Its exclusion “a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle” does not apply: “driver” (DEF-NRS-484A-080, “every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle”) is not read as membership but through the vehicle's controlled motion (the agency reading on s1).

“crossing at grade any track or tracks of a railroad” is a level crossing: st.railway_crossing is the “level crossing of a railway with the roadway, and its nearest rail”; “railroad” (DEF-NRS-484A-200) is “a carrier of persons or property upon cars, other than streetcars, operated upon stationary rails”, and the atom's word “railway” already leaves out a streetcar line laid in the street, which is not a railway level crossing, so no further condition is needed. The subject is crossing from its entry onto the crossing (drv.motion.entering_region, over rel.occupies: “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region”) until it has completely crossed it, which is drv.position.within_clearance_since_entry(x, r) with the clearance s4 states: the concept reads st.region_geometry, “the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it”. The crossing r is the subject's own: anchored by rel.occupies at the entry and by the distance since, never any crossing of the scene.

“to fail to completely cross ... without stopping”: “stopping” is DEF-NRS-484A-260, “any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device”. The halting is drv.motion.halted, “A road user is at a standstill at the observation ... the road user's speed (kin.speed, m/s) is at or below speed_floor ... with no minimum duration”, which keeps “even momentarily”; its own definition id (DEF-NRS-484A-255) is a required stop, but its contract denotes a standstill at an observation whatever the duty, which is what this halting is. A halt while the vehicle is crossing and has not completely crossed is the failure. The definition's exception for a direction of a police officer is carried beside it: dev.human_direction is “a person directing traffic and the direction given; role ∈ {police_officer, ...}; indication ∈ {stop, ...}”, tied to the subject by dev.governs (“the travel regions whose traffic the device controls”) on a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies); dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position, and it is not read as one: it says which road users the direction is given to. The other parts of the definition's exception are read as the narrowings on s3 say.

The section's own definition of “completely cross”: “the trailing end of the vehicle is 15 feet or more past the nearest rail”. Once the body has left the crossing, the point of its outline nearest the crossing is its trailing end, so “trailing end ... 15 feet or more past” is the ground distance from the body outline to the crossing region (st.region_geometry: “the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)”) at or above the literal 15 ft; drv.position.within_clearance_since_entry with clearance 15 ft is true from the entry until that first holds. st.railway_crossing carries the crossing “and its nearest rail”; rel.occupies anchors the entry.

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), and there is a railway level crossing r (st.railway_crossing) that x is crossing and has not completely crossed: drv.position.within_clearance_since_entry(x, r) with clearance the literal 15 ft of s4 — x's footprint entered r (drv.motion.entering_region, over rel.occupies) at the observation or earlier, and at every observation since its body outline has stood less than 15 ft from r (st.region_geometry distance; zero while on r). Read at every observation.
obligation: At every observation at which the applicability holds, x is not halted: drv.motion.halted(x) with speed_floor p.speed_resolution is false (a single observation at a standstill is a halt, since stopping is “any halting, even momentarily”). A halt does not violate where it is in compliance with a police officer's direction: some human direction d (dev.human_direction) with role police_officer and indication stop governs (dev.governs) a travel region l (st.travel_region) x's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) at that observation. The obligation reads x's motion and the direction governing the region x is on; it needs no crossing of its own.

narrowings.why: “the driver of any vehicle” is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the vehicle crossing is taken to be driven, and the duty binds its conduct whoever or whatever is at the controls.

“due to insufficient: (1) Space for the vehicle on the opposite side of the railroad crossing; or (2) Undercarriage clearance of the vehicle” states why the vehicle stops; neither the room it would need beyond the crossing nor its undercarriage clearance over the crossing's profile is observable, so the cause is read through the conduct it explains: a halt while the vehicle is crossing and has not yet completely crossed. A halt on the crossing for another cause (a breakdown) is not told apart.

The posted definition of stopping excepts a halt “necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic”. This section makes a halt due to insufficient space for the vehicle on the opposite side — the space that queued traffic or an object fills — the failure it forbids; reading that exception into it would empty clause (1). The rule therefore does not excuse a halt on the crossing because a road user stands ahead of the vehicle. Of the exception for “the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device”, the police officer's direction to stop is read; no official device directs a halt on the crossing itself (the railway signal or gate directs a halt before it, which a vehicle already crossing has passed, and a signal or stop sign beyond directs a halt at its own line, queueing for which on the tracks is clause (1)), so no device direction is read.

“the nearest rail” is read as the boundary of the crossing region the map carries (st.railway_crossing with its nearest rail): the distance is measured from the body outline to that region, which is at the rail or beyond it.

No human direction is in the scene.

segmentation.text: It is unlawful for any person to drive or operate a vehicle of any kind or character
at: A rate of speed
greater than is reasonable or proper, having due regard for the traffic, surface and width of the highway, the weather and other highway conditions.

elements.justification: “a vehicle of any kind or character”: “vehicle” is DEF-NRS-484A-320, admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle and claimed as the one atom ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (“membership of a legal aggregate”); “of any kind or character” adds no class beyond the definition's. Its exclusion “a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle” does not apply: “any person to drive or operate” is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, drv.motion.moving (“A road user is in motion at the observation: its speed exceeds speed_floor”, over kin.speed), since “a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven”.
“A rate of speed” is kin.speed, the “magnitude of velocity” in m/s; the bound it is held to is the operationalization of s3.

operationalizations.standard: a rate of speed greater than is reasonable or proper, having due regard for the traffic, surface and width of the highway, the weather and other highway conditions
operationalizations.convention: Assured clear distance and design-speed conventions: the stopping sight distance model (a perception-reaction time and a braking deceleration selected by the surface: dry, wet, icy) bounds speed by the sight distance along the road and by the visibility distance; the side-friction convention bounds the speed on a curve by a lateral acceleration; a speed-proportional lateral margin bounds the speed by the room the lane leaves beside the vehicle; a minimum time headway bounds the speed by the gap to traffic ahead in the lane. Each factor's magnitude enters its bound with the speed, so the bound moves with the factor's degree.

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and is moving: drv.motion.moving(x) with speed_floor p.speed_resolution. Read at every observation.
obligation: Surrogate. x's speed v (kin.speed) is not greater than reasonable: every bound below holds at the observation. Let S be x's stopping distance drv.motion.stopping_distance(x; p.perception_reaction_time, a), the deceleration a selected by the surface with Term.cond: p.braking_decel_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds; else p.braking_decel_wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation holds; else p.braking_decel_dry. (1) S is at most the sight distance at x's place (st.sight_distance). (2) S is at most the visibility distance (env.visibility). (3) v times v times the curvature at x's place (st.curvature) is at most p.curve_lateral_accel. (4) For every lane l (st.lane) x's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies): p.lateral_margin_time times v is at most the lane's width (st.lane_width) less x's width (kin.extent, width). (5) For every road user y of the scene that is not x (same) and is ahead of x in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane): p.traffic_time_headway times v is at most the surface gap from x to y (rel.surface_gap).

narrowings.why: “any person to drive or operate” is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a moving vehicle is taken to be driven or operated, and the duty binds its speed whoever or whatever is at the controls.

The traffic (DEF-NRS-484A-285, “pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel”) is read through every road user ahead of the subject in its own lane, whatever its class, by the time gap to it at the subject's speed: a road user in a lane of the highway ahead of the subject is one the speed must regard, so no class condition is read. Traffic crossing, oncoming or beside the road is not read.
The surface is read by a condition that selects the braking deceleration: icy or snow-covered, wet (or precipitation falling), otherwise dry; the degree of grip within each class is not read.

The width of the highway is read through the width of the lane the subject occupies against the subject's own width; the highway's whole width between its boundary lines (st.highway) is not read, and where the subject occupies no lane this factor sets no bound.
The weather is read through precipitation (selecting the wet deceleration) and the visibility distance (the stopping distance kept within it); wind and temperature are not read.

The catch-all “other highway conditions” is read only through the sight distance along the road and the curvature of the road at the subject's place; grade, darkness, crests and obstructions are not read.

The sight distance and the curvature "at x's place" are read at every lane x's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies over st.lane), the region the lane-width bound reads; where x occupies no lane, these two factors set no bound.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A passenger car moves on a dry straight lane in fog at a speed whose stopping distance exceeds the observed visibility distance; the sight distance is long and nothing is ahead in the lane.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The car moves slowly on a dry straight lane of ample width with a long sight distance and visibility, alone in the scene: every bound holds.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The car stands halted at the curb throughout the trace.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As permit, but the source does not observe the visibility distance.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The car moves on an icy road (env.ice_or_snow) at a speed whose stopping distance under the ice deceleration exceeds the sight distance, though under the dry deceleration it would not.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The car takes a tight bend at a speed at which the square of the speed times the curvature exceeds the lateral-acceleration bound; sight and visibility are long.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: The car follows another car ahead in the same lane at a surface gap shorter than the time headway at its speed.

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: A wide truck moves in a narrow lane at a speed whose lateral margin exceeds the room the lane leaves beside it.

param_proposals.name: p.speed_resolution
param_proposals.convention: Sensor resolution: the smallest speed the acquisition standard separates from standstill; a speed at or below it counts as no motion.
param_proposals.source: speed noise of the carla_scene_graph acquisition standard

param_proposals.name: p.perception_reaction_time
param_proposals.convention: Perception-reaction time: the time a driver keeps its speed before braking begins, in the stopping sight distance model.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book, stopping sight distance (brake reaction time)

param_proposals.name: p.braking_decel_dry
param_proposals.convention: Braking deceleration on a dry surface: a firm, controlled stop most drivers make on dry pavement.
param_proposals.source: stopping-distance studies of driver braking on dry pavement (about 0.45 g)

param_proposals.name: p.braking_decel_wet
param_proposals.convention: Design braking deceleration: the deceleration most drivers keep within their lane and control on a wet surface, used by the stopping sight distance model.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book, stopping sight distance (deceleration rate)

param_proposals.name: p.braking_decel_ice
param_proposals.convention: Braking deceleration on an icy or snow-covered surface: the deceleration packed snow or ice allows under controlled braking.
param_proposals.source: winter-road friction measurements (friction coefficient about 0.15)

param_proposals.name: p.curve_lateral_accel
param_proposals.convention: Curve lateral acceleration: the lateral acceleration (speed squared times curvature) above which a curve is taken faster than ordinary drivers' comfort and control margin.
param_proposals.source: side-friction and driver-comfort studies of curve negotiation

param_proposals.name: p.lateral_margin_time
param_proposals.convention: Speed-proportional lateral margin: the lateral room beside a vehicle, both sides together, that grows with speed to absorb lateral wander; the speed times this time must fit in the lane width beyond the vehicle's width.
param_proposals.source: lane-width and lateral-clearance studies of speed choice

param_proposals.name: p.traffic_time_headway
param_proposals.convention: Minimum time headway in traffic: the time gap to the road user ahead in the lane below which the speed is too high for the traffic.
param_proposals.source: car-following headway conventions

segmentation.text: If a highway has been designed to provide
a single right lane to be used only for turning
a vehicle must
Be driven in the right turn lane only for the purpose of making a right turn

elements.justification: st.highway is 'the entire public way between its boundary lines', denoting DEF-NRS-484A-095 ('the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority ...'); st.on_way ('the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on — a lane, roadway, ...') ties the turn lane to that highway. 'has been designed to provide' is the lane's presence on the map (status reading below).

st.turn_lane is 'a lane designated only for turning; side ∈ {left, right}', with side right: 'a ... right lane to be used only for turning'. 'single' is read as no neighbouring lane being a right turn lane too: st.lane_adjacency gives the 'left / right neighbouring lane of the same direction' (its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: the marking between two lanes' is respected: lanes, not markings, are compared), so a pair of adjacent right turn lanes is not a single one.
'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom; 'must' introduces the duty the obligation spans state.

'the right turn lane' is the lane L the condition singles out (st.turn_lane, side right); 'driven in' it is x's footprint overlapping it (rel.occupies). Driving in it other than for the turn shows where x leaves it into the neighbouring lane on its left (st.lane_adjacency, 'left / right neighbouring lane of the same direction') short of the intersection it enters (st.intersection), instead of turning. The right turn the lane serves is made at the intersection L runs into: st.lane_enters ('the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'), an st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet', DEF-NRS-484A-105). 'making a right turn' is read by the heading change of x since its footprint began to overlap that intersection (drv.motion.heading_change_since_entry, integrated from kin.yaw_rate, left positive) reaching minus the turn recognition angle by the time x leaves it; kin.yaw_rate is 'Not a stand-in for: road curvature', and the quantity is compared at the exit, after the whole passage. 'the purpose of' is read through the conduct it explains (reading below).

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and x occupies (rel.occupies) at the observation, or occupied at an earlier observation, a single right turn lane L: an st.turn_lane region of side right lying on (st.on_way) an st.highway region, with no lane adjacent to it (st.lane_adjacency) that is also an st.turn_lane of side right.
obligation: Re-binding L with the same selection and I as the st.intersection region L enters (st.lane_enters): at the observation neither (a) x stops here occupying L (rel.occupies of x and L false here and true at the previous observation) while occupying the lane adjacent to L on its left (st.lane_adjacency) and not occupying I; nor (b) x stops here occupying I, having begun to overlap I at an observation at which it occupied L, and its heading change since that entry (drv.motion.heading_change_since_entry(x, I), step p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph) is greater than minus p.turn_recognition_angle: it left the intersection without turning right.

narrowings.why: 'has been designed to provide' is read through the lane's presence as mapped: a right turn lane on the highway evidences the design.
'Be driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion in the lane, whoever or whatever controls it.

'only for the purpose of making a right turn' is read through the conduct the purpose explains: a vehicle in the lane leaves it either by turning right (into the intersection the lane enters, with a right turn, or off to the right before it); leaving it back into the neighbouring lane on its left short of the intersection, or leaving the intersection it entered from the lane without a right turn, is the lane used for another purpose.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car enters the single right turn lane to pass a queue of through traffic, then moves back into the through lane on its left before reaching the intersection.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car drives in the single right turn lane, enters the intersection the lane runs into and turns a quarter turn to the right before leaving it.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car approaches an intersection on a highway whose approach has no right turn lane.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car enters the intersection from the single right turn lane and leaves it; the source declares kin.yaw_rate absent, so whether it turned right is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car changes back out of the rightmost of two adjacent right turn lanes: the highway provides a dual, not a single, right turn lane.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A car in the single right turn lane drives straight through the intersection and leaves it with its heading unchanged.

param_proposals.name: p.turn_recognition_angle
param_proposals.convention: Turn recognition: the heading change through an intersection beyond which a passage counts as a turn rather than a straight crossing; half the right angle of a turn at a right-angled junction, leaving room for skewed junctions and lane offsets.
param_proposals.source: Intersection geometry conventions (AASHTO Green Book turning paths) and manoeuvre classification in trajectory datasets

segmentation.text: If the driver of a vehicle
intends to turn
at an intersection
and:
The turn is a right turn,
both the approach for the right turn and the right turn must be made from the right turn lane
if the highway has a right turn lane
as set forth in subsection 4 of NRS 484B.223 [NRS-484B-223-4a, NRS-484B-223-4b],
or must be made from the extreme right lane.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway"), claimed by id. 'the driver of' is a role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency).

The intersection the intention is declared at and the turn is made in: st.intersection ("the region where two roadways meet"), entered by x (drv.motion.entering_region: "its footprint overlaps r (rel.occupies) at the observation and did not at the observation before") from the approach carrier it occupies whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters: "the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end").

The turn made is a right turn where the heading change of x since it entered i (drv.motion.heading_change_since_entry: "The signed heading change of road user x since its footprint last began to overlap region r, in degrees, left positive", from kin.yaw_rate) reaches the turn recognition angle to the right. The concept is 'not' a turn by itself; the rule compares it with its bound.

The approach for the turn and the turn are made from the right turn lane R where x's footprint overlaps R (rel.occupies) at its entry into i and at every observation of the approach length of path travelled before it at which x occupies a carrier entering i (a .path window, which reads kin.path_length, "distance travelled along the body's path"). R is the st.turn_lane ("a lane designated only for turning; side ∈ {left, right}") of side right that enters i (st.lane_enters).

The highway has a right turn lane as subsection 4 of NRS 484B.223 sets forth, whose words are borrowed: NRS-484B-223-4a and NRS-484B-223-4b both quote "a single right lane to be used only for turning". That is a st.turn_lane ("a lane designated only for turning") of side right, entering i (st.lane_enters), lying on the same highway (st.on_way: "the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on"; st.highway) as the carrier x approached through, and serving x's direction: its designated direction (st.lane_direction) not opposed to that carrier's (drv.road.opposed_directions false), so that a turn lane on the opposing approach of the same way is not read.

intentions.meaning: The source's current plan for the road user includes a turn, to either hand, at the target region.

compositions.quote: a single right lane to be used only for turning
compositions.why: It borrows only the description of the lane, a single right lane to be used only for turning, to say which lane counts as a right turn lane here; whether a vehicle in that lane complies with paragraph (4)(a), driving in it only to turn right, decides nothing in this duty, so that rule need not apply, hold or be complied with.

compositions.quote: a single right lane to be used only for turning
compositions.why: It borrows only the same description of the lane; whether a vehicle in that lane complies with paragraph (4)(b), not travelling through the intersection, decides nothing in this duty, so that rule need not apply, hold or be complied with.

applicability: x carries ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; at the observation x's right turn in intersection i is recognized: the heading change since x's latest entry into i (drv.motion.heading_change_since_entry(x, i) with step p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph) is at most minus p.turn_recognition_angle there and was not at the observation before; the source declared int.turn for x at i at the observation of that entry (Formula.intent, read through a past operator); and the highway has a right turn lane for x's approach: x entered i from a carrier c with st.lane_enters(c, i) lying on a highway h (st.on_way(c, h)), and some st.turn_lane R of side right enters i (st.lane_enters(R, i)), lies on h (st.on_way(R, h)) and has a designated direction not opposed to c's (drv.road.opposed_directions(R, c) with p.opposed_carriers_cosine false).
obligation: At the observation of that entry into i (read through a past operator), x's footprint overlaps such a lane R, and at every observation of the path window of length p.turn_approach_length behind the entry (measured in x's path, kin.path_length) at which x occupies a carrier entering i, it occupies that R: both the approach and the turn are made from the right turn lane.

narrowings.why: 'the driver of a vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

'the approach for the right turn' is read as the stretch of path, of the approach length, just before the entry into the intersection, during which every carrier of the intersection x is on must be the right turn lane; a lane change into the turn lane earlier than that stretch complies.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: x (ru.motor_vehicle) approaches i on a through lane c of highway h whose approach also has a right st.turn_lane R entering i; int.turn is declared for x at i; x enters i from c and turns right beyond p.turn_recognition_angle.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same highway; x, with int.turn declared at i, is on R for the whole approach length before its entry, enters i from R and turns right.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: x, with int.turn declared at i, turns left in i (heading change positive beyond p.turn_recognition_angle).

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: x turns right in i from a through lane with int.turn declared, but the source does not record which intersection the turn lane beside it enters, so whether the highway has a right turn lane for this approach is unknown.

param_proposals.name: p.turn_recognition_angle
param_proposals.convention: Turn recognition: the heading change through an intersection beyond which a passage counts as a turn rather than a straight crossing; half the right angle of a turn at a right-angled junction, leaving room for skewed junctions and lane offsets.
param_proposals.source: intersection geometry design conventions (AASHTO Green Book)

param_proposals.name: p.opposed_carriers_cosine
param_proposals.convention: Direction tolerance: minus the cosine of the narrowest angle between two carriers' designated directions that counts as opposite directions; carriers within about 45 degrees of exactly opposed count.
param_proposals.source: road-network direction conventions of map data

param_proposals.name: p.turn_approach_length
param_proposals.convention: Turn approach: the distance travelled just before entering an intersection over which a turning vehicle's approach is judged; about two passenger-car lengths, shorter than the storage of a short turn bay.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book turn-lane storage practice

segmentation.text: When a vehicle enters an intersection
controlled by a traffic-control signal which is installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered, but is inoperative at the time the vehicle enters the intersection,
the driver of the vehicle

shall proceed as if a stop sign had been erected at each entrance to the intersection and shall stop at a clearly marked stop line or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is none, at the point nearest the intersection
where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.
After making such a stop,
the driver shall proceed
cautiously,
yielding to vehicles
which have previously completed a stop
or are within the intersection.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle.
