'enters an intersection' is drv.motion.entering_region on a region of kind st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet'; DEF-NRS-484A-105 'the area embraced within the prolongation ... of the lateral curb lines'; the alley junction its (3) excludes is excluded by the atom's own contract), read through rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'. st.intersection is not a stand-in for a crosswalk or stop line: the entry is into the junction itself.

dev.traffic_signal 'a signal head' is the traffic-control signal (DEF-NRS-484A-290 'by which traffic is alternately directed to stop or proceed'); dev.inoperative 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication' carries 'installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered, but is inoperative' word for word. 'controlled by' is dev.governs 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection': the signal governs the intersection or the approach carrier (st.lane_enters 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into', a carrier of kind st.travel_region the subject occupies); dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position and none is read from it. 'at the time the vehicle enters' fixes the reading to the entry observation.

'the driver of the vehicle': the duty binds the vehicle's controlled motion (DEF-NRS-484A-080 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle'), read through the vehicle of the admitted aggregate; who controls it is not observable.

'shall stop' is a required stop, DEF-NRS-484A-255 'complete cessation from movement', carried by drv.motion.halted over kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity'. 'proceed as if a stop sign had been erected at each entrance' states the halt a stop sign requires (dev.stop_sign 'regulatory sign requiring a full halt') together with the yield of the next sentence; no sign is erected, so no device is read: the halt carries it here and the yield is the other node's. 'at a clearly marked stop line': st.stop_line 'the transverse line marking where vehicles halt', tied to the subject's approach by st.entrance_of 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks', read on the same carrier (of kind st.travel_region) as st.lane_enters (distance never stands for belonging); nearness by st.region_geometry 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it' (not a stand-in for occupancy, which is not read from it), side by prim.region_offset_along 'measured along a carrier's designated direction'. 'before entering the crosswalk on the near side': st.crosswalk 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection' (DEF-NRS-484A-065 both parts) that st.entrance_of records as marking the approach carrier, with rel.occupies of it false at the halt; st.crosswalk is not a stand-in for a stop line. 'at the point nearest the intersection': a halt with the footprint outside the st.intersection (rel.occupies false), its distance read by st.region_geometry; st.intersection is not a stand-in for the crosswalk or stop line absent on this branch.

operationalizations.standard: a view of approaching traffic on the through highway: how much of the crossing way must be in view
operationalizations.convention: Intersection sight distance for a stop-controlled approach (AASHTO Green Book case B): from the halt, the crossing way (a st.highway on which the intersection lies, st.on_way, and the approach carrier does not) is in view for at least p.intersection_sight_distance in the smaller of its two directions (st.sight_along_way 'the distance along a way ... within which another vehicle on that way could be seen from the road user's eye ... the smaller of the two directions'). st.sight_along_way is not a stand-in for whether an actual road user is seen: the view of approaching traffic is the view along the way whether or not traffic is present.

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and enters an intersection i (st.intersection) at this observation (drv.motion.entering_region x i) through an approach carrier c: a region of kind st.travel_region that x occupies at this observation with st.lane_enters c i. At this observation some traffic signal d (dev.traffic_signal) that governs i or c (dev.governs d i, or dev.governs d c) is inoperative (dev.inoperative d). Where x occupies several carriers entering i and the verdict differs between them, which governs is unknown; a rule never picks the carrier that favours x.
obligation: Act: x halted (drv.motion.halted x with p.speed_resolution) at the place the words name, taken in their order, on the approach that leads to this entry. Place: (1) where a stop line s (st.stop_line) is recorded as marking c (st.entrance_of s c): at s, an observation at which x is halted, its body within p.stop_point_tolerance of s (st_region_geometry_distance x s) and s not behind x along c's designated direction (prim.region_offset_along x s c at least zero); (2) where the source observes the stop lines' entrances and none marks c, and a crosswalk w is recorded as marking c (st.entrance_of w c): before entering w, an observation at which x is halted, its footprint not overlapping w (rel.occupies x w false), its body within p.stop_point_tolerance of w and w ahead of x along c (prim.region_offset_along x w c positive); (3) where the source observes that no stop line and no crosswalk marks c: an observation at which x is halted with its footprint outside i (rel.occupies x i false), within p.stop_point_tolerance of i, or farther upstream where a highway h on which i lies and c does not (st.on_way i h; st.on_way c h false) is in view from x for at least p.intersection_sight_distance (st_sight_along_way x h). History bound (the ontology's approach convention): the search runs back from this entry and ends at the approach start, the last observation before the entry at which x, on c, is outside the governing place's stopping zone upstream (not on the place, short of it along c by prim.region_offset_along, and farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance by st_region_geometry_distance; for place (3) the place is c's entrance end at i), or at x's previous entry into i, whichever is later. A halt found in that stretch meets the duty; reaching either end without one violates it; reaching neither (the recording begins inside the approach) leaves it unknown. A halt before the previous entry into i never counts for this entry. An observed exit from the stopping zone upstream begins a new approach and the halt is owed again; crossing the mark, moving on, a change of carrier or a lateral move within this entry, a reverse that stays within the zone and speed noise begin none. Missing evidence: whether this is an entry through c is unknown where the observation before it does not show x on a mapped carrier; where a stop line's or crosswalk's association with c is unobserved, whether it governs is unknown; where the association lists are observed and exclude c, the next place in the words' order governs and the duty is not unknown on that ground; a recorded halt at a place known to govern decides compliance whatever else is missing.

narrowings.why: 'traffic-control signal' is an official device (DEF-NRS-484A-290 'placed or erected by a public authority or railroad'); the signal head's presence on the road is read as that status.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.
'clearly marked' is read through the represented stop line; paint clarity is not modelled, and which place governs, the halt and its timing are unchanged.

'the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view': a halt within p.stop_point_tolerance of the intersection counts, and a halt farther upstream counts where the view bound holds there; that no nearer point with the view existed is not checked, since no atom compares points along the approach for their view.

'the through highway' at an intersection whose signal is dark is read as a highway the intersection lies on that the subject's approach carrier does not lie on (st.on_way): every entrance is treated as stop-controlled, so the crossing way is the one whose traffic the driver must see; its designation as a through highway is a status no feature shows here.

The history bound's 'previous entry into i' is read at x's exit from i after that entry (the observation at which rel.occupies x i turns false): a halt x makes while its footprint still overlaps i after a previous entry does not count for this entry.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: x (motor vehicle class, member of the vehicle aggregate) drives on lane c with st.lane_enters c i; stop line s with st.entrance_of s c; dev.traffic_signal d governs i and is dev.inoperative. x is first observed 80 m upstream of s at 12 m/s, keeps kin.speed above 3 m/s past s and enters i.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but x halts (kin.speed 0) with its body 0.5 m short of s, s ahead along c, then moves on and enters i.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but d shows circular_green and dev.inoperative is false at x's entry into i.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the source does not observe dev.inoperative for d.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: No stop line marks c (the line list is observed); crosswalk w with st.entrance_of w c; d inoperative. x halts with its footprint overlapping w, then enters i: the halt is not before entering the crosswalk and no other halt occurs on the approach.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: No stop line and no crosswalk marks c; d inoperative. x halts outside i, 1 m from it, then enters i.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the recording begins with x already on c 1.5 m short of s at 1 m/s, inside the stopping zone; no halt is recorded before x enters i.
scenarios.boundary: x's approach start on c, the last observation outside the stopping zone upstream of s, lies before the recording.

param_proposals.name: p.speed_resolution
param_proposals.convention: Sensor resolution: the smallest speed the acquisition standard separates from standstill; a speed at or below it counts as no motion.
param_proposals.source: carla_scene_graph acquisition standard: speed resolution of the recorded kinematics

param_proposals.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Stop-point tolerance: the largest ground distance between a halted body and the line, crossing or intersection edge at which the halt counts as made at that place; a body farther upstream is outside the stopping zone.
param_proposals.source: MUTCD 2009 section 3B.16 stop-line placement (at least 4 ft ahead of the crosswalk) and vehicle positioning variability at a stop

param_proposals.name: p.intersection_sight_distance
param_proposals.convention: Intersection sight distance: the length of the crossing way, in the smaller of its two directions, that a driver halted on a stop-controlled approach must be able to see to judge a gap in approaching traffic.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets (2018) section 9.5.3, case B departure sight triangles at a low urban design speed

segmentation.text: If the driver of a vehicle
intends to turn
at an intersection
and:
The turn is a right turn,
both the approach for the right turn and the right turn must be made from the right turn lane
if the highway has a right turn lane
as set forth in subsection 4 of NRS 484B.223 [NRS-484B-223-4a, NRS-484B-223-4b],
or must be made from the extreme right lane.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway"), claimed by id. 'the driver of' is a role read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
st.intersection ("the region where two roadways meet"), entered by x (drv.motion.entering_region) from the approach carrier whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters).
A right turn: the heading change since x entered i (drv.motion.heading_change_since_entry, "in degrees, left positive", from kin.yaw_rate) reaches the turn recognition angle to the right.

Read negated here: the 'or' alternative applies where the highway has no right turn lane as subsection 4 of NRS 484B.223 sets forth, borrowing "a single right lane to be used only for turning" (NRS-484B-223-4a, NRS-484B-223-4b): no st.turn_lane of side right enters i (st.lane_enters) on the same highway (st.on_way, st.highway) with a designated direction (st.lane_direction) not opposed to x's approach (drv.road.opposed_directions).

The extreme right lane: a st.lane entering i whose ordinal within the carriageway equals the count of lanes in its direction (st.lane_adjacency: "lane ordinal within the carriageway and the count of lanes in that direction; ordinal 1 is the leftmost lane, looking along the lane's direction"). The approach and the turn are made from it where x's footprint overlaps it (rel.occupies) at the entry and over the approach length of path before it (.path window, kin.path_length). Lane adjacency is 'not a stand-in' for a marking and is not used as one.

intentions.meaning: The source's current plan for the road user includes a turn, to either hand, at the target region.

compositions.quote: a single right lane to be used only for turning
compositions.why: It borrows only the description of the lane, a single right lane to be used only for turning, to say which lane counts as a right turn lane, here to establish that there is none; whether a vehicle complies with paragraph (4)(a) decides nothing in this duty, so that rule need not apply, hold or be complied with.

compositions.quote: a single right lane to be used only for turning
compositions.why: It borrows only the same description of the lane; whether a vehicle complies with paragraph (4)(b) decides nothing in this duty, so that rule need not apply, hold or be complied with.

applicability: x carries ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; at the observation x's right turn in intersection i is recognized (drv.motion.heading_change_since_entry(x, i) with step p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph at most minus p.turn_recognition_angle there and not at the observation before); int.turn was declared for x at i at the observation of its latest entry into i (read through a past operator); x entered i from a carrier c with st.lane_enters(c, i) on highway h (st.on_way(c, h)); and no st.turn_lane of side right enters i on h with a designated direction not opposed to c's (drv.road.opposed_directions with p.opposed_carriers_cosine).
obligation: At the observation of that entry into i (read through a past operator), x's footprint overlaps a st.lane L that enters i (st.lane_enters(L, i)), lies on h, has a designated direction not opposed to c's, and whose st.lane_adjacency ordinal equals its lane count (the rightmost lane looking along its direction); and at every observation of the path window of length p.turn_approach_length behind the entry (kin.path_length) at which x occupies a carrier entering i, it occupies that L.

narrowings.why: 'the driver of a vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

'the extreme right lane' is read as the lane whose ordinal equals the count of lanes in its direction on the approach; the approach is the stretch of path of the approach length before the entry. An approach with no lanes mapped has no such lane, and the duty is not decided there.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: x (ru.motor_vehicle) approaches i on a two-lane approach with no right turn lane, in the leftmost lane; int.turn is declared at i; x turns right from that lane.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same approach; x is in the lane whose ordinal equals the lane count for the whole approach length, enters i from it and turns right.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The approach has a right st.turn_lane entering i on the same highway in x's direction; x turns right (NRS_484B_400_1_o1 governs that case).

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: x turns right from a two-lane approach with no right turn lane, with int.turn declared, but the source does not observe lane ordinals and counts.

param_proposals.name: p.turn_recognition_angle
param_proposals.convention: Turn recognition: the heading change through an intersection beyond which a passage counts as a turn rather than a straight crossing; half the right angle of a turn at a right-angled junction, leaving room for skewed junctions and lane offsets.
param_proposals.source: intersection geometry design conventions (AASHTO Green Book)

param_proposals.name: p.opposed_carriers_cosine
param_proposals.convention: Direction tolerance: minus the cosine of the narrowest angle between two carriers' designated directions that counts as opposite directions; carriers within about 45 degrees of exactly opposed count.
param_proposals.source: road-network direction conventions of map data

param_proposals.name: p.turn_approach_length
param_proposals.convention: Turn approach: the distance travelled just before entering an intersection over which a turning vehicle's approach is judged; about two passenger-car lengths, shorter than the storage of a short turn bay.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book turn-lane storage practice

segmentation.text: When a vehicle enters an intersection
controlled by a traffic-control signal which is installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered, but is inoperative at the time the vehicle enters the intersection,
the driver of the vehicle
shall proceed as if a stop sign had been erected at each entrance to the intersection and shall stop
at a clearly marked stop line
or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection
or, if there is none, at the point nearest the intersection
where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.
After making such a stop,
the driver shall proceed
cautiously,
yielding to vehicles
which have previously completed a stop
or are within the intersection.

elements.justification: As in NRS_484B_250_4_o1: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'enters an intersection' is drv.motion.entering_region on a st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet') through rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'.

As in NRS_484B_250_4_o1: dev.inoperative 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication' of a dev.traffic_signal that governs ('the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection') the intersection or the approach carrier (st.lane_enters) x occupies, read at the entry.
'the driver of the vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (DEF-NRS-484A-080).

'shall proceed' after the stop is the subject's entry into the intersection (drv.motion.entering_region, rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'): the observation at which it proceeds in preference to others or not.

'yielding to vehicles' (DEF-NRS-484A-210 right-of-way 'the right ... to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another vehicle'): x does not enter the intersection while a vehicle of the admitted aggregate is owed precedence; the yield is read at x's entry.

'which have previously completed a stop': another vehicle y halted (drv.motion.halted, DEF-NRS-484A-255 'complete cessation from movement') on another approach carrier of the intersection (st.lane_enters 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into', rel.occupies) before x's own halt began, and has stayed on that carrier outside the intersection since.
'are within the intersection': rel.occupies of y and the intersection x enters, at x's entry.

operationalizations.convention: Surrogate safety measure of a conflict (FHWA SSAM): at x's entry, no other road user's centre is predicted, under constant velocities, to come within p.conflict_clearance of x's within p.immediate_hazard_gap. The primitives are not a stand-in for contact or the danger of a crash by themselves; the bound the parameters set is the standard's.

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and enters intersection i (st.intersection) at this observation (drv.motion.entering_region x i) through an approach carrier c (st.travel_region, x occupies c, st.lane_enters c i); a traffic signal (dev.traffic_signal) that governs i or c (dev.governs) is dev.inoperative at this observation; and NRS_484B_250_4_o1 is complied with for x at this observation (rule NRS_484B_250_4_o1 {x -> x}). That rule is engaged at exactly this entry, so its compliance here is the fact 'such a stop' refers to: x halted, on the approach to this entry, at the place it requires.
obligation: At this entry: (1) no vehicle y other than x (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) occupies i (rel.occupies y i); (2) no vehicle y other than x waits on another approach carrier c2 of i (st.travel_region, st.lane_enters c2 i, x not on c2) having completed a stop before x: y has occupied c2 and not i at every observation since an observation at which x's halt on c began (x halted, drv.motion.halted with p.speed_resolution, and on c there, and not halted at the observation before) and y was already halted on c2 (halted there and at the observation before); (3) proceeding cautiously: no road user z other than x is in predicted conflict with x, i.e. not both prim.closest_approach_within x z with horizon p.immediate_hazard_gap and prim.closest_approach_distance x z with the same horizon below p.conflict_clearance.

narrowings.why: The signal head's presence is read as the official status of the traffic-control signal.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
'cautiously' names no factor; it is read only through the predicted conflict at the entry, and marked surrogate as a standard of care.
The yield is judged at x's entry into the intersection: an entry while a vehicle is owed precedence is the failure to yield; conduct after the entry is not read for this yield.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Signal d governing i is dev.inoperative; x halts within 0.5 m of the stop line marking its lane c, then enters i while vehicle y occupies i.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but x is the only road user in the scene when it enters i after its halt.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: Signal d shows circular_green (not dev.inoperative) when x enters i.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but rel.occupies of y and i is not observed at x's entry.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: x halts at its stop line; vehicle y had halted at the stop line of crossing carrier c2 two seconds before x's halt began and still waits there, outside i; x enters i first.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but x halted 30 m upstream of the stop line marking c (outside the stopping zone) and rolled through the line: the halt was not such a stop, NRS_484B_250_4_o1 is not complied with, and this duty does not arise.

param_proposals.name: p.speed_resolution
param_proposals.convention: Sensor resolution: the smallest speed the acquisition standard separates from standstill; a speed at or below it counts as no motion.
param_proposals.source: carla_scene_graph acquisition standard: speed resolution of the recorded kinematics

param_proposals.name: p.immediate_hazard_gap
param_proposals.convention: Critical gap: the time within which another road user's arrival at the conflict area, or its predicted closest approach, counts as an immediate hazard to a road user about to cross or join its path.
param_proposals.source: HCM 7th ed. Exhibit 20-11 base critical headway (major-street left turn)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Conflict radius: the centre distance at predicted closest approach below which two road users' paths count as in conflict; about the half-length plus half-width of two passenger cars.
param_proposals.source: FHWA Surrogate Safety Assessment Model (Gettman et al. 2008) conflict definition

segmentation.text: Except when traffic is being controlled by a police officer or a traffic-control signal:
When proper signs have been erected,
the driver of a vehicle

shall stop or yield at a clearly marked stop line or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is none, then at the point nearest the intersection
where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.
After having stopped or, in the event of a yield sign, slowed or stopped,
the driver shall yield the right-of-way
to other vehicles which have entered the intersection from such through highway
or which are approaching so closely on such through highway as to constitute an immediate hazard during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection.

elements.justification: 'traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic; the traffic whose control matters is the subject's own flow, so x is read as a member. 'being controlled by a police officer' is dev.human_direction 'a person directing traffic' with role police_officer (DEF-NRS-484A-180 'every officer authorized to direct or regulate traffic') governing the intersection or x's approach carrier (dev.governs); 'or a traffic-control signal' is a dev.traffic_signal governing them that is not dev.inoperative ('showing no valid indication'): a dark signal controls nothing, and NRS 484B.250(4) then governs.

'proper signs' are dev.stop_sign ('regulatory sign requiring a full halt') or dev.yield_sign ('regulatory sign requiring yielding without a mandatory halt') governing (dev.governs) x's approach carrier c (rel.occupies, st.lane_enters c i) or the intersection; the duty is owed on the approach to x's entry into the intersection (drv.motion.entering_region).
'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'the driver' is read through its controlled motion.

'stop' (required: DEF-NRS-484A-255 'complete cessation from movement') is drv.motion.halted; 'or yield' at a yield sign is, by the words of the next sentence ('in the event of a yield sign, slowed or stopped'), a halt or slowing (drv.motion.slowing: forward motion with kin.accel_longitudinal below minus the resolution); kin.accel_longitudinal is not a stand-in for speed, and both are read. The places are read as in NRS_484B_250_4_o1: st.stop_line recorded by st.entrance_of as marking x's approach carrier (st.lane_enters, st.travel_region), nearness by st.region_geometry, side by prim.region_offset_along along the carrier's direction; else the st.crosswalk st.entrance_of records as marking that carrier, with the halt's footprint not overlapping it (rel.occupies); else a halt with the footprint outside the st.intersection.

operationalizations.standard: a view of approaching traffic on the through highway: how much of the through highway must be in view
operationalizations.convention: Intersection sight distance for a stop- or yield-controlled approach (AASHTO Green Book cases B and C): from the place of the act, the through highway (a st.highway on which the intersection lies, st.on_way, and the subject's approach carrier does not) is in view for at least p.intersection_sight_distance (st.sight_along_way, the smaller of its two directions); not a stand-in for whether an actual road user is seen.

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and enters intersection i (st.intersection) at this observation (drv.motion.entering_region x i) through an approach carrier c it occupies (st.travel_region, st.lane_enters c i); a dev.stop_sign or dev.yield_sign governs c or i (dev.governs) at this observation; and traffic is not being controlled by a police officer or a traffic-control signal: x being a member of traffic (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic), no dev.human_direction with role police_officer and no dev.traffic_signal that is not dev.inoperative governs c or i at this observation. Where x occupies several carriers entering i and the verdict differs between them, which governs is unknown.
obligation: Act: where a dev.stop_sign governs c or i, x halted (drv.motion.halted x with p.speed_resolution) at the place; where only a dev.yield_sign governs, x halted at the place or was slowing (drv.motion.slowing x with p.speed_resolution and p.deceleration_resolution) at some observation of the approach before passing the place (before the place is behind x along c by prim.region_offset_along; for place (3), before x enters i). Place, in the words' order: (1) where a stop line s (st.stop_line) is recorded as marking c (st.entrance_of s c): at s, x's body within p.stop_point_tolerance of s (st_region_geometry_distance) and s not behind x along c (prim.region_offset_along x s c at least zero); (2) where the source observes that no stop line marks c and a crosswalk w is recorded as marking c (st.entrance_of w c): before entering w, x's footprint not overlapping w, within p.stop_point_tolerance of w and w ahead along c; (3) where the source observes that neither marks c: x's footprint outside i, within p.stop_point_tolerance of i, or farther upstream where a highway h on which i lies and c does not (st.on_way i h; st.on_way c h false) is in view from x for at least p.intersection_sight_distance (st_sight_along_way x h). History bound (the approach convention): the search runs back from this entry to the approach start, the last observation before the entry at which x, on c, is outside the governing place's stopping zone upstream (not on it, short of it along c, farther than p.stop_point_tolerance), or to x's previous entry into i, whichever is later; the act found there meets the duty, reaching either end without it violates it, reaching neither leaves it unknown. An act before the previous entry into i never counts; an observed exit from the stopping zone upstream begins a new approach; crossing the mark, a change of carrier, a lateral move, a reverse within the zone and speed noise begin none. Missing evidence: whether this is an entry through c is unknown where the observation before it does not show x on a mapped carrier; a mark whose association with c is unobserved governs unknown; where the lists are observed and exclude c, the next place governs; a recorded act at a place known to govern decides compliance whatever else is missing.

narrowings.why: 'traffic is being controlled' is read as control of x's own approach or of the intersection it enters, x being a member of the traffic aggregate; the officer's role and the signal's presence are read as their official status.
'proper signs' are read through the presence of a stop or yield sign governing the approach or the intersection.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
At a yield sign the act owed at the place is read as the 'slowed or stopped' the next sentence names; yielding to traffic is the other node's duty.
'clearly marked' is read through the represented stop line.
A halt within p.stop_point_tolerance of the intersection counts, and one farther upstream counts where the view bound holds; that no nearer point with the view existed is not checked.
'the through highway' is read as a highway the intersection lies on that the subject's signed approach carrier does not lie on; its designation is presumed from the sign on the subject's approach.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: dev.stop_sign governs lane c (st.lane_enters c i); stop line s marks c; no officer and no signal. x is first observed 80 m upstream at 12 m/s, never falls to the speed resolution and enters i.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but x halts with its body 0.5 m short of s, then enters i.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: No sign governs c or i; x enters i without halting.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but dev.governs is not observed for the stop sign.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: dev.yield_sign governs c; x, moving forward at 10 m/s, decelerates at 2 m/s² 30 m upstream of s and enters i at 4 m/s without halting.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but a dev.human_direction with role police_officer governs i while x rolls through.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the recording begins with x 1.5 m short of s at 1 m/s; no halt is recorded before x enters i.
scenarios.boundary: x's approach start on c, the last observation outside the stopping zone upstream of s, lies before the recording.

param_proposals.name: p.speed_resolution
param_proposals.convention: Sensor resolution: the smallest speed the acquisition standard separates from standstill; a speed at or below it counts as no motion.
param_proposals.source: carla_scene_graph acquisition standard: speed resolution of the recorded kinematics

param_proposals.name: p.deceleration_resolution
param_proposals.convention: Sensor resolution: the smallest longitudinal deceleration the acquisition standard separates from steady speed; a deceleration at or below it counts as no slowing.
param_proposals.source: carla_scene_graph acquisition standard: acceleration resolution of the recorded kinematics

param_proposals.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Stop-point tolerance: the largest ground distance between a halted body and the line, crossing or intersection edge at which the halt counts as made at that place; a body farther upstream is outside the stopping zone.
param_proposals.source: MUTCD 2009 section 3B.16 stop-line placement (at least 4 ft ahead of the crosswalk) and vehicle positioning variability at a stop

param_proposals.name: p.intersection_sight_distance
param_proposals.convention: Intersection sight distance: the length of the crossing way, in the smaller of its two directions, that a driver halted on a stop-controlled approach must be able to see to judge a gap in approaching traffic.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets (2018) section 9.5.3, case B departure sight triangles at a low urban design speed

segmentation.text: An operator of a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
upon a roadway
shall give all signals by hand and arm
in the manner required by NRS 484B.420 [DEF-NRS-484B-420],
except that the operator may give a signal for a right turn by extending his or her right hand and arm horizontally and to the right side of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter.

elements.justification: The three terms are the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle (“a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride”), DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle (“a device upon which a person may ride, having two or three wheels ... an electric motor which produces not more than 750 watts”) and DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter (“a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor”), each claimed as one ru.aggregate atom (“membership of a legal aggregate”), the same mapping the index records for “The operator of a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter”. The defined word keeps its definition's qualifications: DEF-NRS-484B-018 admits only a vehicle that “(1) Must not weigh more than 100 pounds without a rider; and (2) Must have a maximum speed of not more than 20 miles per hour when powered solely by its electric motor”, which no atom observes, so the run's reading leaves ru.electric_scooter unresolved under that id and ru.aggregate is, by its contract, “unknown when no included class holds and the user carries an unresolved class”: a rider of an electric scooter only is judged unknown, never compliant or violated. ru.electric_scooter (“a standing or seated electric scooter with handlebars”) is not claimed in its place, since it would drop the definition's weight and speed limits and the aggregate's contract excludes expanding an admitted aggregate into a class. The exclusion “a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle” does not apply: “An operator” is read through the device's controlled motion (agency reading).

“roadway” is DEF-NRS-484A-220, “that portion of a highway which is improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder”: st.roadway is “the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder”, the definition's whole extent; “upon” is rel.occupies, “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region”. The roadway is not a stand-in for the sidewalk, which the rule does not read as roadway.

“give all signals by hand and arm”: sig.hand_signal is “a driver's or rider's arm signal; meaning ∈ {no_signal, left, right, stop_or_slow, re_enter}”, whose meanings are exactly those NRS 484B.420 sets forth in the words s4 borrows: “(1) Left turn: Hand and arm extended horizontally. (2) Right turn: Hand and arm extended upward. (3) Stop or decrease speed: Hand and arm extended downward. (4) Reentering lane of traffic from parked position: Hand and arm extended horizontally.” A signal the rider gives otherwise is a lit turn indicator, sig.turn_indicator, “state ∈ {off, left, right}”; its exclusion (“the turn or lane change itself”) does not apply, since the rule reads the signal, not the turn. “all signals” is every signal the rider shows: where an indicator is lit, an arm signal of the same meaning must be given with it; where only an arm signal is given, it is given by hand and arm. Left horizontal serves both a left turn and reentering, so an indicator to the left is matched by either meaning.

The permitted right-turn form, “extending his or her right hand and arm horizontally and to the right side”, is an arm signal whose meaning is a right turn: sig.hand_signal records “the meaning of the one given”, so it reads right, as the form of NRS 484B.420 does; the exception admits it as a signal given in the required manner, and the rule accepts an arm signal of meaning right however it is formed.

compositions.quote: (1) Left turn: Hand and arm extended horizontally. (2) Right turn: Hand and arm extended upward. (3) Stop or decrease speed: Hand and arm extended downward. (4) Reentering lane of traffic from parked position: Hand and arm extended horizontally.

applicability: x is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter (ru.aggregate; membership of the electric-scooter aggregate is unknown where its definition's weight and speed limits decide it, as the run's reading classifies it); x's footprint overlaps a roadway (rel.occupies, st.roadway); and x gives a signal: its turn indicator (sig.turn_indicator) is left or right, or its arm signal (sig.hand_signal) is other than no_signal. Read at every observation.
obligation: x gives the signal by hand and arm: sig.hand_signal(x) is other than no_signal; where sig.turn_indicator(x) is left, sig.hand_signal(x) is left or re_enter; where sig.turn_indicator(x) is right, sig.hand_signal(x) is right (the posture of NRS 484B.420 or the right-arm form of the exception, both read as meaning right).

narrowings.why: “An operator” is read through the device's controlled motion: the rider of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter on the roadway is the one whose signals are judged, whoever is at the controls.

The manner of NRS 484B.420 is read through the meaning the source decodes from the arm signal: which arm is extended and on which side are not observed (sig.hand_signal records the meaning only), so an arm signal is taken as given in the required manner when its meaning is one of the four the section sets forth. “All signals” is read as every signal the rider shows, an arm signal or a lit turn indicator; hazard lamps are not read as a signal.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: An electric bicycle rider on a roadway shows a lit right turn indicator and gives no arm signal (sig.hand_signal no_signal).

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rider on a roadway gives an arm signal of meaning left, with no indicator lit.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rider on a roadway gives no signal: no indicator lit and no arm signal.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the source does not observe arm signals.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: An electric bicycle rider on a roadway shows a lit right indicator and extends the right arm horizontally to the right side; the source decodes the arm signal as meaning right.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: An electric bicycle rider on a roadway shows a lit right indicator while giving an arm signal of meaning left.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: An electric bicycle rider on a sidewalk, not on the roadway, shows a lit right indicator with no arm signal.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
about to enter or exit a controlled-access highway
shall yield the right-of-way
to all vehicles approaching on the highway
whose proximity constitutes an immediate hazard
and shall continue to yield the right-of-way
to that traffic
until the driver may proceed with reasonable safety.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); 'the driver' is a relational role, read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency narrowing).

As in NRS_484B_263_o1: st.controlled_access 'a highway with access only at designated points, and its entrance and exit lanes'; 'about to enter or exit' is read by the entry (drv.motion.entering_region: 'its footprint overlaps r at the observation and did not at the observation before') or the exit (drv.motion.leaving_region) over rel.occupies.

As in NRS_484B_263_o1: other vehicles of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle whose footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) the same controlled-access region a ('on the highway') and that are in motion (drv.motion.moving: 'its speed exceeds speed_floor', kin.speed), i.e. 'approaching on the highway'.

'shall continue to yield the right-of-way ... until the driver may proceed': x holds back its entry or exit until it can be made with the safety margin; the entry (drv.motion.entering_region) or exit (drv.motion.leaving_region) over rel.occupies is the observation at which x proceeds, and the duty is judged there.

'that traffic' refers back to the vehicles approaching on the highway (s4); 'traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('vehicles ... using any highway for purposes of travel'), each such vehicle read as a member of it, beside the s4 conditions it keeps.

operationalizations.convention: Safe merge headway (two-second rule, HCM freeway merge gap acceptance): at the entry or exit, every approaching vehicle of that traffic (prim.closest_approach_within over the critical-gap horizon p.immediate_hazard_gap) is at a surface gap from x (rel.surface_gap 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies') of at least its own speed (kin.speed) times p.merge_time_headway, so the margin grows with the approaching vehicle's speed.

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and at this observation enters (drv.motion.entering_region x a) or leaves (drv.motion.leaving_region x a) a region a of kind st.controlled_access.
obligation: For every region a of kind st.controlled_access that x enters (drv.motion.entering_region x a) or leaves (drv.motion.leaving_region x a) at this observation (the applicability's selection written again), every road user y other than x that is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and a member of that traffic (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic), occupies a (rel.occupies y a), is moving (drv.motion.moving y with p.speed_resolution) and approaches x (prim.closest_approach_within x y with horizon p.immediate_hazard_gap) is at a surface gap from x (rel.surface_gap x y) of at least y's speed (kin.speed y) times p.merge_time_headway.

narrowings.why: 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
'about to enter or exit' is read by the entry into or exit from the controlled-access region.
Continuing to yield until the driver may proceed is read at the entry or exit observation: the manoeuvre is made only when the safety margin holds.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: x enters controlled-access region a at 15 m/s while vehicle y in a, moving at 30 m/s and approaching x, is at rel.surface_gap 20 m (needed 60 m).

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: x enters a as the only road user in the scene.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: x drives on an arterial; no st.controlled_access region is entered or left.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but kin.speed is not observed: whether y is moving and the speed-proportional margin it is owed are both unknown, while the gap stays 20 m.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: x enters a while y, approaching at 30 m/s, is at rel.surface_gap 90 m.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
shall not make a U-turn
in an area designated as a school zone or school crossing zone
except:
(a) When there are no children present;
(b) On a day on which school is not in session;
(c) During the period from a half hour after school is no longer in operation to a half hour before school is next in operation;
(d) If the zone is designated by an operational speed limit beacon,
during the hours when the pupils of the school are in class
and the yellow lights of the speed limit beacon are not flashing in the manner which indicates that the speed limit is in effect;
or
(e) If the zone is not designated by an operational speed limit beacon,
during the times when the sign designating the school zone or school crossing zone indicates that the speed limit is not in effect.

As used in this section, “speed limit beacon” means a device which is used in conjunction with a sign and equipped with two or more yellow lights that flash alternately to indicate when the speed limit in a school zone or school crossing zone is in effect.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway", with its exceptions), claimed by id. 'The driver of' names who controls it (DEF-NRS-484A-080, "every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle"), a role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency), not a membership.

'U-turn' is defined by DEF-NRS-484B-077 ("the turning of a vehicle upon a highway so as to proceed in the opposite direction, whether accomplished by one continuous movement or not"); the accepted concept drv.motion.u_turn carries that definition (its contract quotes it, DEF-NRS-484B-077), recognizing the reversal of x's heading over the window behind the observation. The concept reads the heading change itself, so the rule states the act only through the concept and claims no atom or primitive of its own for this span. The place, upon a highway inside the zone, is stated by span d3.

A school zone or school crossing zone (DEF-NRS-484B-063 "those sections of streets which are adjacent to school property"; DEF-NRS-484B-060) is a legal region class that is also marked on the road; the ontology's section on what is not an atom: "Where the same category is also marked on the road by a sign (dev.zone_sign), the sign is the atom and the category is not." dev.zone_sign: "a sign that begins or ends a signed zone along the road; kind ∈ {school, school_crossing, ...}". The area designated is the travel regions the sign governs (dev.governs: "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls"), and x is in it where its footprint overlaps one (rel.occupies). dev.zone_sign is 'not a stand-in' for whether its condition holds now; that is read only in span d13 through prim.conditions_hold.

Children present in the zone: a road user of class ru.child ("pedestrian who is visibly a child") whose body lies within the presence reach of a travel region the zone sign governs (st.region_geometry: "the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)"), so that children on the sidewalks beside the zone's lanes count. A reach relates the region to the child, not two regions. No children present: no such road user.

The zone designated by a speed limit beacon: a dev.speed_limit_beacon ("a pair or more of yellow lamps mounted with a speed sign, flashing alternately when the sign's limit is in effect", which is the section's own definition in span d14) governing (dev.governs) the travel region x occupies (rel.occupies) or a region the zone sign governs. 'operational' is read through the beacon's presence (observable_reading status).
dev.speed_limit_beacon "flashing attribute": the beacon's lights not flashing in the manner that indicates the limit is in effect is its flashing attribute false.
A zone not designated by a speed limit beacon: no dev.speed_limit_beacon governs (dev.governs) the travel region x occupies or a region the zone sign governs.

The sign designating the zone is the dev.zone_sign of span d3, whose "conditions attribute: a structured reading of the sign's legend" states when its limit is in effect; that it indicates the limit is not in effect is prim.conditions_hold ("the structured conditions of a device ... hold at the observation for a road user") false for x. The sign is 'not a stand-in' for the condition holding, which is why the primitive reads it.

assumptions.meaning: The calendar day of the observation is one on which the school the zone serves is not in session, as declared for the map or the trace.

The time of the observation lies at least a half hour after the school the zone serves last ceased operation and at least a half hour before it next begins operation, as declared for the map or the trace.
The time of the observation lies within the hours during which the pupils of the school the zone serves are in class, as declared for the map or the trace.

residues.why: The section's own definition of a speed limit beacon; dev.speed_limit_beacon's contract ("a pair or more of yellow lamps mounted with a speed sign, flashing alternately when the sign's limit is in effect") already states it, and the elements of spans d8, d10 and d12 read that atom; it imposes no duty of its own.

applicability: x carries ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; at the observation x's U-turn is recognized (drv.motion.u_turn(x) with p.u_turn_window and p.u_turn_reversal_tolerance rises there); and at some observation of that act (an observation within p.u_turn_window behind the recognition at which x yaws, drv.motion.yawing with p.yaw_rate_resolution) x's footprint overlapped a travel region r governed (dev.governs) by a dev.zone_sign z of kind school or school_crossing that is not an end sign.
obligation: The U-turn is made only where one exception covers the whole act: for each zone sign z selected as in the applicability, one of the alternatives below holds at every observation of the act (each observation within p.u_turn_window behind the recognition at which x yaws). (a) No road user of class ru.child lies within p.child_presence_reach (st.region_geometry distance) of a travel region z governs. (b) asm.school_not_in_session_day holds. (c) asm.outside_school_operation_margin holds. (d) A dev.speed_limit_beacon governs the region x occupies or a region z governs, asm.pupils_in_class holds, and that beacon is not flashing. (e) No dev.speed_limit_beacon governs the region x occupies or a region z governs, and z's conditions do not hold for x (prim.conditions_hold false). Where none of them covers the whole act, the duty is violated.

narrowings.why: 'The driver of a vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.
'an area designated as a school zone or school crossing zone' is read through the zone sign on the road and the travel regions it governs; the designation is presumed from the sign's presence.
'operational' is read through the beacon's presence governing the zone's regions; a beacon that is installed but out of order is not told apart.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: x (ru.motor_vehicle) makes a U-turn on a lane governed by a school zone sign z; a ru.child stands within p.child_presence_reach of z's lane at every observation, asm.school_not_in_session_day and asm.outside_school_operation_margin are declared false, and a speed limit beacon governing the lane is flashing.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: x makes a U-turn on z's lane while no ru.child lies within p.child_presence_reach of any region z governs at any observation of the act.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: x makes a U-turn on a street no school zone or school crossing zone sign governs.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: x drives along z's lane with children on the sidewalk and turns about, but its yaw rate is missing, so whether a U-turn was made is unknown.

scenarios.name: occasion_d3
scenarios.narrative: Baseline as in forbid (children present, school in session, inside the operation margin, beacon flashing): x begins its U-turn on z's lane and completes it on a lane beyond the stretch z governs; it occupied z's lane for part of the act only.

scenarios.name: occasion_d3_outside
scenarios.narrative: x drove along z's lane, left the governed stretch, and only afterwards, on a lane no zone sign governs, makes its U-turn: it was in the zone before the act began only.

scenarios.name: occasion_d5
scenarios.narrative: U-turn on z's lane; no ru.child is within p.child_presence_reach at the first observations of the act, then a child walks up beside the lane before the act is recognized; the other alternatives fail throughout.

scenarios.name: occasion_d5_outside
scenarios.narrative: Children stood beside z's lane before the act began and left; at every observation of the U-turn none lies within p.child_presence_reach; the other alternatives fail.

scenarios.name: occasion_d8
scenarios.narrative: A beacon governs the region x occupies at the start of the U-turn only; x ends the turn on a region no beacon governs; asm.pupils_in_class holds and the beacon is not flashing; z's conditions hold; children present, school in session, inside the margin: neither (d) nor (e) covers the whole act.

scenarios.name: occasion_d8_outside
scenarios.narrative: No beacon governs the region x occupied before the act; a non-flashing beacon governs every region x occupies during the U-turn and asm.pupils_in_class holds throughout it; children present.

scenarios.name: occasion_d10
scenarios.narrative: A beacon governs z's lane and asm.pupils_in_class holds throughout; the beacon is not flashing for the first part of the U-turn and flashing for the rest; children present.

scenarios.name: occasion_d10_outside
scenarios.narrative: A beacon governs z's lane and asm.pupils_in_class holds throughout; the beacon was flashing before the act and is not flashing at any observation of the U-turn; children present.

scenarios.name: occasion_d12
scenarios.narrative: No beacon governs the region x occupies at the start of the U-turn, a flashing beacon governs the region it ends on; z's conditions do not hold throughout; children present, school in session, inside the margin.

scenarios.name: occasion_d12_outside
scenarios.narrative: A beacon governed the region x occupied before the act; no beacon governs any region x occupies or z governs during the U-turn; z's conditions do not hold throughout; children present.

scenarios.name: occasion_d13
scenarios.narrative: No beacon; env.civil_time leaves z's posted window during the U-turn, so z's conditions do not hold for the first part of the act and hold for the rest; children present, school in session, inside the margin.

scenarios.name: occasion_d13_outside
scenarios.narrative: No beacon; z's conditions held before the act and do not hold at any observation of the U-turn; children present.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: x makes a U-turn on z's lane with children present while asm.school_not_in_session_day is declared true at every observation of the act.

under_way.justification: An observation inside the act is one within the U-turn window behind the recognition at which x's heading is changing (drv.motion.yawing: "the absolute value of its yaw rate exceeds yaw_floor", kin.yaw_rate): the turning is motion, and x occupied the zone's lanes before the turning began, so no region alone tells the act apart.

param_proposals.name: p.u_turn_window
param_proposals.convention: U-turn recognition window: the longest time over which a reversal of heading, made in one movement or in several forward and backing movements, is recognized as one turning; a multi-point turn on a narrow street.
param_proposals.source: observed durations of three-point turns (naturalistic driving studies)

param_proposals.name: p.u_turn_reversal_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Reversal tolerance: the largest difference between the size of the heading change over the window and a half turn within which the road user counts as proceeding in the opposite direction; covers the offset of a turn into a lane of the opposite direction and heading noise.
param_proposals.source: trajectory-classification practice for U-turn detection

param_proposals.name: p.yaw_rate_resolution
param_proposals.convention: Sensor resolution: the smallest yaw rate the acquisition standard separates from a straight path; a yaw rate at or below it counts as no heading change.
param_proposals.source: yaw-rate resolution of the carla_scene_graph acquisition standard

param_proposals.name: p.child_presence_reach
param_proposals.convention: Presence reach: the ground distance from a child's body to a travel region of a school zone within which the child counts as present in the zone; the width of a sidewalk and verge beside the roadway.
param_proposals.source: urban street cross-section conventions (sidewalk and buffer widths)
